title: Hallucinations suggest experience can come from higher-order activity

statements.text: Prefrontal stimulation, dopaminergic drugs and schizophrenia can yield visual hallucinations, and rare Charles Bonnet cases with damaged primary visual cortex have vivid ones. If experience can exist without first-order representations, its qualitative character might depend entirely on higher-order ones.

sources.quote: Thus conscious visual awareness, albeit hallucinatory, evidently can result from activity in prefrontal cortex.
If conscious experience can exist in the absence of first-order representations, the qualitative character of conscious awareness might depend entirely on higher-order representations.
